newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada not considering new aid for Canadian.
newsitem.headline: Canada not considering new aid for Canadian.

text.p: Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson repeated on Thursday that the federal government was not considering assistance or relaxed investment regulations for financially endangered Canadian Airlines.
"The company is currently engaged in a restructuring process, and it is important for that to succeed," Anderson told reporters on arriving at a cabinet meeting.
"The company has not requested any aid, and therefore we're not considering assistance at this time."
He did not address the fact that the two biggest unions serving Canadian have asked Ottawa to bail the airline out.

Anderson said it was still the position that no request had been received from American Airlines, Canadian Airlines or any other organization with respect to increasing American investment in Canadian Airlines.
"We have had no request. We have not considered it...If such a request were received, we'd look at it, but that doesn't mean to say we'd accept it," he said.
American Airlines parent AMR Corp would require a government exemption from foreign ownership rules to increase its minority shareholding in Canadian.
